$comment: Benchmark dataset RECIPE - the committed description of what to build.
This file contains NO character data, NO market data, and NO databases. It
names blueprints by SDE typeID, which is stable across every install, so any
developer can check out the repo, run `npm run bench:build`, log in their own
characters, and get a benchmark environment exercising the same code paths.
PORTABILITY: a developer who owns none of these blueprints still gets a valid
run. resolveOwnedBlueprint() (blueprint-calculator.js:357) returns null for an
unowned blueprint and the app falls back to ME 0 + built. The numbers differ
between developers; the code paths exercised do not. That is the accepted
tradeoff - see docs/PROFILING.md on comparability scope.
SIZE LADDER: plans are sized to span roughly 8 to 735 material nodes, modelled
on real plans. The spread is itself a measurement: timings that scale linearly
with node count indicate a constant-factor problem, while super-linear scaling
indicates an algorithmic one (the reverse linear scans at
manufacturing-plans.js:3495,3682 are a live O(n^2) suspect). Those two
diagnoses call for completely different fixes.
Only TOP-LEVEL blueprints are listed. Intermediates are detected and created by
the app itself during recalculation, which is deliberate - the seeder must not
hand-build the tree, or it would stop reflecting how the app actually works.
NOTE on useIntermediates: this is NOT part of addBlueprintToPlan's parameter
object - that call silently drops unknown keys. It defaults to 'raw_materials'
and the builder applies any other value through updatePlanBlueprint, whose
allowedFields list is snake_case (use_intermediates).
TO CHANGE THE DATASET: edit this file, then re-run `npm run bench:build`.
`npm run bench` hashes this file and refuses to run against a stale dataset.

invention.$comment: findBestDecryptor evaluates 9 options x 2 cost calls x ~11 materials, which market-read-cache.js documents as ~198 calculateRealisticPrice calls for ~11 distinct items. A T2 cruiser blueprint is the canonical case.

$comment: Market data is FETCHED into the sandbox during bench:build, not committed -
the live market database is ~329MB. Real order books matter because
calculateVWAP, calculatePercentilePrice, removeOutliers and
getBestPriceWithMinVolume all branch on book shape, so synthetic books risk
exercising the wrong branches.
The type list is derived from the plans above after they are built, so it
needs no maintenance here. The region is The Forge (Jita), the default
reference market.
